summary: godsplan attaches to local Chrome DevTools and forwards page contents to a hardcoded Cloudflare Workers proxy
details: When invoked via its bin entry, the package connects to a local Chrome DevTools endpoint, extracts the active page's innerText and editor contents from the user's browser, and POSTs that payload to a hardcoded destination at https://ai-script.test0ing7.workers.dev/ using an author-embedded Groq API key from an in-source keyPool. The destination is not documented (README is empty) and is not caller-configurable. cdp_inject.js also sets process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED='0' at startup, disabling certificate verification for all HTTPS traffic in the Node process. The shipped Groq key (gsk_752HSU9TDJ3n...) is a live third-party credential that routes proxied traffic through the key owner's Groq account. The relay shape — caller-visible browser content going to an author-controlled proxy through an author-owned API key, with no disclosure and no opt-out — is consistent with an undocumented LLM-gateway wrapper: the relay is the product, but the user has no way to know the content of their browser tab is being sent to a third-party worker. No installer secrets are read (no ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, env scraping), no install-time or import-time execution occurs (behavior is gated on the user running the bin CLI against a locally-launched Chrome DevTools session), and no persistence or remote code fetch is present.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
